detail.title: W114 exchange-wall Compass rotation
detail.description:
New exact search equivalence from independent external even-degree Fermat census, with arithmetic edges rechecked locally.

W114 wall:
A=(1,7,78,79,86,91)
B=(1,13,43,72,103,110)
C=(1,13,43,80,102,103)

External source reports these three are a complete claim-equivalence triangle under exchange moves and remain unresolved by its closure family. We independently reconstructed exact exchanges:

A -> B:
unit 85 on B gives (2,7,78,79,85,91).
Shared S=(7,78,79,91).
Exchanger q_AB=(1,29,86,112), grade-2 across all units.

A -> C:
unit 79 on C gives (1,43,50,78,79,91).
Shared S=(1,78,79,91).
Exchanger q_AC=(7,64,71,86), grade-2.

B -> C:
shared S=(1,13,43,103).
Exchanger q_BC=(12,34,72,110), grade-2 and Galois/permutation equivalent to a p=3 Aoki-standard surface character.

More structured A -> C 3-entry exchange:
shared S=(1,79,91);
A-rem=(7,78,86), C'-rem=(43,50,78);
q=(7,36,64,71,78,86),
which splits into zero-sum triples (7,36,71) and (64,78,86), so the exchanger is \*-split.

Search policy:
Any explicit carrier found for A, B, or C is eligible as a candidate after explicitly compiling the exchange correspondence back to A. Do not transfer evidence from the external census without receiver-local verification.

Negative calibration:
All three have identical weighted exponent complexity {114,114,114,114,57,19}; all fail pair-separated weighted cancellation and simple pair-CI screens. The rotation expands the search presentation but does not trivialize the geometry.
